item.title: Akea Brionne: Time Bends for the Tender @ Lyles & King, NYC
item.description: Lyles & King is pleased to present Time Bends for the Tender, a solo exhibition of Akea Brionne's work on view through February 21, 2026. Drawing inspiration from bell hooks’ Sisters of the Yam, this series explores the interior landscape of black women cultivated in order to survive the psychic, social, and geographic pressures placed upon them.

item.title: Israel Campos "Echoes" @ Charlie James Gallery, Los Angeles
item.description: Charlie James Gallery is pleased to present Israel Campos: Echoes, the artist’s first exhibition with the gallery. Campos excavates the layered cultural histories of Los Angeles using a combined painting and screenprinting technique. In his role as artist-historian, Campos reveals the figures, stories, and myths that echo through the city’s history, folding Mexican folklore into its fabric and often drawing from primary texts for narrative and stylistic inspiration. item.title: Christian Rex van Minnen "Metanoia" @ Nanzuka Underground, Tokyo
item.description: NANZUKA is pleased to present “Metanoia,” a solo exhibition of new works by Christian Rex van Minnen at NANZUKA UNDERGROUND. This exhibition marks the artist’s second solo show at NANZUKA following his first exhibition in Japan which was held simultaneously across three venues (NANZUKA UNDERGROUND, 3110NZ by LDH Kitchen, NANZUKA 2G) in 2021.

item.title: Katelyn Ledford "Verso" @ Fredericks & Freiser, New York
item.description: Fredericks & Freiser is pleased to present an exhibition of new paintings by Katelyn Ledford. Known for virtuosic trompe-l’oeil and dark humor, Ledford constructs images where artifice, vulnerability, and bravado collide. Working exclusively with oil and acrylic on canvas, she renders wood grain, masking tape, lace, and denim with the charged aura of stage props. In her hands, illusion becomes performance.

item.title: Golden Days: Dabin Ahn @ François Ghebaly, Los Angeles
item.description: François Ghebaly is proud to present Golden Days, Dabin Ahn’s solo exhibition at the gallery’s Los Angeles space. Painter and sculptor Dabin Ahn transforms personal objects, Korean ceramic vessels, and other ephemeral still-life elements into sites of passage. item.title: Annie Pendergrast "Taut" @ Megan Mulrooney, Los Angeles
item.description: Megan Mulrooney is pleased to present Taut, our first solo exhibition of abstracted still life paintings with Los Angeles-based artist Annie Pendergrast. Flowers, vases, stripes, grids, and looping forms recur across the exhibition, rendered in precise gradients and graphic color combinations. item.title: Deadly Prey: Movie Posters from Ghana @ Harman Projects, San Francisco
item.description: Harman Projects, in conjunction with Spoke Art and Deadly Prey Gallery, is pleased to announce an exhibition of hand-painted movie posters from Ghana. The origin of this artistic movement has its roots in the 1980s with the rise of mobile cinemas across the country of Ghana. item.title: Robert Williams: Fearless Depictions @ Long Beach Museum of Art, Long Beach
item.description: The Long Beach Museum of Art is pleased to present Jux founder Robert Williams: Fearless Depictions, a survey exhibition featuring 57 paintings spanning from 2001 to the present, along with two large-scale sculptures by the iconic Southern California artist. Robert Williams’ epic, cartoon-inspired history paintings draw deeply from American vernacular culture and its visual slang, using concrete, relatable, and often absurd imagery to deliver sharp social commentary.

item.title: Oscar Murillo: "el pozo de agua" @ kurimanzutto, Mexico City
item.description: OSCAR MURILLO (b. 1986, La Paila, Colombia) has developed a multifaceted and challenging practice that spans painting, collaborative projects, video, sound and installation. Through each body of work, the artist probes ideas of collectivity and shared culture, demonstrating a commitment to the power of material presence alongside complex meditations on contemporary society.
